summary: IDS feed s060_single is degraded: 4.8% of frames (157/3292) exceed the IDS 1518-byte MTU (up to 8058 bytes) and are dropped by the IDS NIC, creating a detection blind spot.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo/oversize frames up to 8058 bytes to a 1 Gbps IDS port with 1518-byte maximum frame size. The IDS network interface drops any frame larger than its MTU at ingress before the IDS engine sees it.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS loses 4.8% of traffic before inspection (157 of 3292 frames). Attacks, exfiltration or C2 carried in large frames are invisible to the IDS, reducing detection coverage and allowing MTU-based evasion. IDS requires full payload so loss is not recoverable.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs_full_payload=true, so broker slicing would break detection. Align MTUs: enable jumbo frames (e.g., 9000+ bytes) on the IDS port/NIC and path, or if not possible configure the packet broker to fragment or soft-truncate oversize frames to 1518 bytes for this tool port.
